why:
phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): on `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode` too, forwarding to the engine; `register_on_*` takes `CallbackReturn (*)(const State&, void*)` plus a context, not a `std::function`.

Before phase-482 W4: RE-VERDICTED phase-417 W4.f. was `gap`, and the capability now SHIPS: `LifecycleNode::register_on_shutdown(callback, context)` runs `callback` instead of the `on_shutdown` virtual, so a ported node registers a transition callback rather than subclassing -- which C (`rclc_executor_lifecycle_register_on_*`) and Rust (`LifecyclePollingNode::register_on_*`) had all along and C++ did not, even though `register_services()` already called the FFI's own `register_on_*` one layer down. THE DIVERGENCE IS THE CALLBACK TYPE: upstream takes a `std::function<CallbackReturn(const State&)>`, which allocates; ours is a `CallbackReturn (*)(LifecycleState, void*)` plus a context, because six `std::function`s stored on this class would need an allocator AND would make `sizeof(LifecycleNode)` depend on a capability probe, which `check-cpp-capability-layout` forbids. `previous` is the `LifecycleState` enum rather than a `rclcpp_lifecycle::State` object for the reason `cpp:Transition` records. The callback is stored HERE and the trampoline picks it over the virtual, so registering before or after `register_services()` behaves the same and there is still exactly one registrant at the C seam; registering at the FFI directly would let `register_services()` silently overwrite a callback set first.
